project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas field-learning set with B030 canonical bluestem anchors
project_scope.note: The family lesson still teaches transferable grass anatomy first. B030 adds a local inflorescence-architecture comparison using canonical big bluestem and bushy bluestem, while broomsedge remains comparison-only on a project range HOLD.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at the culm and collar zone: find a true node, a leaf sheath wrapped around the culm, and a ligule where sheath becomes blade. In flower, read the whole inflorescence before dissecting a spikelet.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Grass culms usually have conspicuous solid nodes with internodes between them; leaves are typically two-ranked and differentiated into sheath, collar/ligule zone and blade.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: The basic reproductive unit is the spikelet. One or more florets sit above one or more glumes; each floret is subtended/enclosed by a lemma and palea, with awns or hairs useful in many genera.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Caryopsis (grain), often retained with surrounding lemma/palea or other persistent spikelet parts.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Use two doors. Vegetative plant: node → sheath → collar/ligule → hairs → growth form. Flowering plant: whole inflorescence → branch/raceme arrangement → one spikelet → glumes → lemma/palea → awn/hairs.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: node/collar → inflorescence silhouette → spikelet anatomy → local bluestem architecture → vegetative tie-breakers
visual_lesson.intro: Learn a grass twice: first as a whole plant and again as a spikelet. The B030 bluestems make the middle step—inflorescence architecture—especially visual.

steps.title: 1 · Find a real grass node
steps.look_for: A jointed culm with a leaf sheath originating at a conspicuous node.
steps.why_it_matters: This puts you into the grass workflow before you ever name the species.

steps.title: 2 · Read the collar zone
steps.look_for: Where the sheath ends and the blade begins: inspect the ligule, collar, hairs and any auricles.
steps.why_it_matters: For nonflowering grasses, this is one of the highest-value identification zones.

steps.title: 3 · Read the whole inflorescence before zooming in
steps.look_for: Big bluestem = a few exposed fingerlike racemes; bushy bluestem = a dense, broad, fluffy crown of many clustered units.
steps.why_it_matters: Architecture can separate these local bluestems at arm's length before tiny spikelet characters are visible.

steps.title: 4 · Isolate one spikelet
steps.look_for: Glumes outside the florets; lemma and palea around an individual floret; then note awns, hairs and fertility.
steps.why_it_matters: Spikelet structure is the reproductive language that transfers across Poaceae.

steps.title: 5 · Compare eight bluestems and Indiangrass by raceme origin, node and collar
steps.photo_role: big vs bushy vs broomsedge architecture
steps.look_for: Long fingers (KR); stout turkey-foot fingers (big); separate SHORT racemes (little); broad brush (bushy); white nodal BEARD + fan (cane); narrow cotton (silver); elongated panicle + rifle-sight ligule (Indiangrass); sheathed broomsedge racemes.
steps.why_it_matters: For restoration crews distinguishing introduced KR from native-lookalike bluestems, head architecture and same-plant nodes/collars reduce accidental native removals.

steps.title: 6 · Use collar and habit as tie-breakers
steps.look_for: After architecture, return to ligule/collar hairs, blade width, sheath hairiness, tillering and rhizome/stolon habit.
steps.why_it_matters: These characters keep the learner from relying on fall color, fluffiness or one distant silhouette.

comparisons.title: Grass vs sedge vs rush
comparisons.rule: Grass: conspicuous nodes plus sheath/collar/ligule and spikelets built from glumes, lemma and palea. Sedge: commonly solid culms, often 3-ranked leaves and spikelets without the grass floret architecture. Rush: commonly round solid node-poor stems with small flowers bearing 6 tepals. Treat these as field doors, not exception-free laws.

comparisons.title: Big bluestem vs bushy bluestem
comparisons.rule: Andropogon gerardi has a few exposed digitate racemes—the turkey-foot pattern. Anatherum glomeratum has a dense fluffy broomlike crown formed by many short silky racemes.

comparisons.title: Flowering vs vegetative doors
comparisons.rule: Flowering: silhouette → branch/raceme pattern → spikelet → glumes → lemma/palea → awn/hairs. Vegetative: node → sheath → collar → ligule → hairs → blade width → tiller/rhizome/stolon.

comparisons.title: KR vs cane vs silver
comparisons.rule: KR has several long slender terminal fingers; cane has a broad fan and heavily BEARDED nodes; silver has a narrow cottony head made of >10 SHORT rames and normally pale smooth nodes. Node hair presence/absence alone does not prove KR.

comparisons.title: Little vs big vs bushy bluestem
comparisons.rule: LITTLE carries short silky racemes on different upper leafy branches; BIG exposes fewer stout turkey-foot fingers; BUSHY makes a broad dense brushlike crown of short paired spathe-associated rames.

comparisons.title: Indiangrass and broomsedge
comparisons.rule: INDIANGRASS has one branched elongated panicle and a conspicuous membranous rifle-sight ligule; BROOMSEDGE has narrow silky raceme units individually associated with flattened upper spathe-like sheaths.

visual_lesson.caveat: Never trust flower color, fall-red stems or white fuzz alone. Existing historical county claims should not be recalculated here: B. torreyana remains UNRESOLVED; B. barbinodis's stored PASS cites two counties outside the project's approved zone (Williamson and Val Verde), so its range certification awaits a separate source audit. Field identification remains independent from project native metrics.

bluestem_photo_atlas.title: Central Texas bluestem and Indiangrass — 8 encountered species
bluestem_photo_atlas.first_decision: Does the upper head form long terminal fingers, separate short silky racemes, a broad brush/fan, or one panicle? Photograph head origin and true nodes.

species.first_look: Several LONG thin fingerlike racemes in a terminal cluster; stiff papilla-based hairs on upper leaf blade near collar support ID
species.caution: Introductory invasive/introduced comparison. Node hairs variable; do NOT use hairless nodes as decisive.

species.first_look: MANY SHORT silky racemes occur separately on branching upper leafy stems; often a tight clump
species.caution: Do not ID from autumn red color alone.

species.first_look: Usually 2–6 relatively STOUT exposed racemes near one terminal point, often turkey-foot
species.caution: KR can also have multiple terminal fingers; compare stoutness, branching and leaf collar.

species.first_look: Dense broad BRUSH of crowded short silky paired racemes, subtended by spathe-like leafy sheaths
species.caution: Can resemble broomsedge or silver bluestem before flowering is fully developed.

species.first_look: Dense long soft hair BEARD at stem nodes plus broad FAN of many silvery branches
species.caution: Node must be from the same flowering plant; a fuzzy head alone is insufficient.

species.first_look: Narrow contracted COTTONY SILVER head of >10 short rames; pale usually smooth nodes
species.caution: This project currently has native-range UNRESOLVED, not target-zone certified PASS.

species.first_look: Single narrow-to-open golden BRANCHED PANICLE and conspicuous pointed membranous 'rifle-sight' ligule
species.caution: Examine attached fertile spikelet and sterile pedicel; panicle color alone not enough.

species.first_look: Relatively narrow silky inflorescence of paired rames partly held in long flattened spathe-like sheaths
species.caution: Existing species is canonical; compare directly against bushy bluestem.

decision_flow.question: One golden elongated BRANCHED panicle and tall rifle-sight membranous ligule?
Several exposed fingers near one terminal point?
decision_flow.yes: KR if thin/long and stiff hairs near collar; big bluestem if fewer stout turkey-foot fingers; inspect spikelets.

decision_flow.question: Short silky racemes repeated on separate upper leafy branches?
decision_flow.no: Check brushy, fanlike, or cottony head and stem nodes.

decision_flow.question: Dramatic soft white hair beard around true stem nodes?
decision_flow.yes: Bothriochloa barbinodis candidate; broad fan supports
decision_flow.no: Narrow cottony densely short-branched head suggests B. torreyana; broad compact brush with spathes suggests Anatherum glomeratum.

decision_flow.question: Narrow individually spathe-held hairy units rather than broad bushy crown?
decision_flow.no: Unresolved: sample attached fertile spikelets, collar and node; label bluestem sp.

bluestem_photo_atlas.management_caution: Never make KR removal decisions from head fluff or fall color alone; do a genuine head+collar+stem node exam. Avoid exposing held photos or making county native certification from provisional comparison taxa.

canonical_species.look_for: Tall prairie bunchgrass with usually 2–6 exposed fingerlike racemes radiating near the culm tip; the classic three-raceme form makes a turkey-foot.
Dense broad broomlike or cottony clusters near the top, built from many short paired rames with long silky hairs and partly enclosed by upper sheaths.

comparison_only_hold.status: range HOLD — not a canonical project anchor
comparison_only_hold.look_for: Narrower silky racemes more individually tucked within flattened spathe-like upper sheaths; useful as a visual tie-breaker but not yet promoted.

canonical_anchor_set.taxonomy_note: Current project taxonomy follows the B030 Kew/POWO reconciliation: big bluestem remains Andropogon, while bushy bluestem and broomsedge are treated in Anatherum. Familiar Andropogon names remain searchable aliases.

family_confusion_cleanup.field_question: If this looks grass-like, which family is it and what single structure breaks the tie?

comparison_matrix.first_lock: Jointed culm with conspicuous nodes; blade-sheath junction has a ligule.
comparison_matrix.confirm: Spikelet has grass floret architecture: glumes outside, lemma + palea around each floret; fruit is a caryopsis.
comparison_matrix.do_not_overtrust: Hollow stems or round stems alone.

comparison_matrix.first_lock: Often solid culm, commonly 3-ranked leaves and closed sheaths; stem may be triangular, round, or flattened.
comparison_matrix.confirm: Minute flower subtended by a single scale; perianth absent/reduced; one hard one-seeded nutlet/achene. Carex adds a perigynium.

comparison_matrix.first_lock: Grass/sedge-like habit but individual flowers still look like tiny conventional flowers.
comparison_matrix.confirm: Six persistent tepals surrounding a superior ovary; fruit is a capsule with several seeds.

decision_key: Can you see conspicuous culm nodes plus a sheath-blade junction with a ligule? → Poaceae door.
No obvious grass node/ligule? Inspect one reproductive unit.
Six tepals around a real flower and later a multi-seeded capsule? → Juncaceae.
Flower reduced beneath a scale and fruit a single nutlet/achene? → Cyperaceae.
exception_locks: Triangular stem supports Cyperaceae but never proves it.
Round stem does not prove Juncaceae.
A grass may have solid internodes; use nodes + ligule + spikelet architecture.
Vegetative plants may remain family-uncertain until the collar/sheath or reproductive unit is visible.

family_confusion_cleanup.genus_routing_note: After family confirmation, route first by whole inflorescence architecture, then collar/ligule and spikelet characters; do not route genera from fall color or general fuzziness.
